versions.changelog: Add end-of-run 'report platform friction' feedback step (fb_8s2h7m87tg).

**Version 2.2.0 summary:** Adds reporting of platform friction/limitations after each run; file only if an actual issue occurred.

- Introduces a new "Before you exit — report platform friction" section, instructing users to report platform/tool limitations (e.g., schema gaps, dirty data, dedup issues, unclear errors, workarounds, failed uploads, etc.) via the `publish` tool as feedback, but only if a real issue was encountered.
- Specifies: do not file empty/duplicate reports; at most one feedback call per run.
- Removed the separate skill-card.md file (no longer included).
- Core extraction and deduplication procedure remains unchanged.

- Added support for topic-focused extraction: `next_unmethoded_literature` now accepts an optional `keyword` to filter papers by topic or field.
- Instructions updated to guide using the `keyword` parameter for area-specific method extraction and explain behavior when no matches are found.
- Minor documentation clarifications to support the new feature.
- Removed redundant file: skill-card.md.

**2.0.0 – Major update: Enforces at most one method per kind per paper and changes how literature-method links are tracked.**

- Limit: Now allows at most one method of each kind (paradigm, approach, technique, algorithm, model) per paper. When there are multiple candidates for a kind, retain only the most important one.
- Deduplication change: Instead of bumping attention counts on existing method entries (bump_attention), now link papers to existing methods via `link_method_literature`.
- Validation: The `kind` field must be exactly one of the five supported values to avoid publishing errors.
- Reporting: Now records and reports all literature-method links created for deduplicated methods.
- Documentation: All procedures and examples updated in SKILL.md and method-rubric to reflect new logic and constraints.
- Housekeeping: Removed obsolete `skill-card.md`.
Initial release: extract research methods (paradigms, approaches, techniques, algorithms, models) from literature, one paper per run; dedupe against existing methods and bump attention on duplicates.
